theorem: Define the explicit weighted 5x5 grid R_* below. For EVERY complex kernel line contained in span{|3>,|4>} on Alice OR Bob, its rank-four local projection of R_* has Schmidt number <=2, even if the opposite local map is arbitrary. R_* is PPT and SN3, so these are actual PPT outputs. More generally the same SN bound holds for every operator alpha*R_*+T with alpha>=0 and T any nonnegative sum of the ten other grid-generator projectors; if this larger operator is PPT, all its outputs in the stated family are PPT. No generic two-non-coordinate-kernel or arbitrary 4x4 claim is made.
source: [q]=|q><q|; A=|02>+|11>+|20>, V=|01>, W=|10>, B=|12>+|34>, C=|21>+|43>, Q=|22>+|33>. Set R_*=[A]+[00]+4[V]+4[W]+[B]+[14]+[C]+[Q]+2[23]+2[32]+[41]. Its trace24, exact 25x25 PPT calculation and SN3 range argument are in frontier-20261028-grid55-weighted-coordinate-theorem-v1.json SHA256 f1e892255a20d6c3b23afa42994a5fe90feea3be1cb63979a135e6da3ea702c6; the range/SN3 source is https://arxiv.org/html/2402.12966v1 Figure 2 and Appendix B. R_* is invariant under swapping Alice and Bob because its paired weights agree.
kernel_charts: Use the Alice chart K|0,1,2,4>=|0,1,2,3>, K|3>=t|3>, with kernel span{|3>-t|4>}; write U=|t|^2. At t=0 this is a coordinate deletion covered in frontier-20261028-grid55-one-coordinate-arbitrary-opposite-v1.json SHA256 d17fe2163bd7181e00af10ae6a3a5a933b355a06dad3866e52ee32a252a122a1. For U>=1/3, rescale the output fourth coordinate to the other chart K3=|3>, K4=(1/t)|3>; the Gram criterion in frontier-20261028-grid55-tail-mixture-v1.json SHA256 50848412e0a220537da080e48c226c308b5151df35273e5db50385fecab736b6 applies because |1/t|^2<=3. The remaining case 0<U<=1/3 is treated below; both endpoints are included.
small_t_parameters: Let s=U^(1/3), p=1-s, a=1/sqrt(p), w=2/sqrt(s), c=s^(3/2)/2 and lambda=(p/s)*t. For 0<U<=1/3, 0<s<=3/4 and 0<p<1. The Alice projections satisfy C'=|21>+|33>, Q'=|22>+t|33>; hence Q'-tC'=|22>-t|21> and C'-Q'/t=|21>-|22>/t. V'=|01>, W'=|10>, and |00> remains unchanged.
two_four_phase_seeds: For z^4=1 define b_z=(A'-tV')+z*a|00>+conjugate(z)*a^(-1)(Q'-tC') and c_z=(A'+lambda V')+z*w W'+conjugate(z)*c(C'-Q'/t). The nonzero head rows of b_z are [z*a,-t,1], [0,1,0], [1,-t*conjugate(z)/a,conjugate(z)/a]; the last row is (conjugate(z)/a) times the first, and Alice row3 vanishes. Thus SR(b_z)<=2. The head determinant of c_z is (1+lambda/t)*w*c-1=0 since 1+lambda/t=1/s and w*c=s; its fourth row also vanishes. Thus SR(c_z)<=2. Four-phase orthogonality gives T_b=[A'-tV']+a^2[00]+a^(-2)[Q'-tC'] and T_c=[A'+lambda V']+w^2[W']+c^2[C'-Q'/t].
coupled_gram: The mixture p*T_b+s*T_c consumes [A']+U*p/s[V']+[00]+4[W'] and a rank-one Gram subtraction from [C']+[Q']. Cross terms between A' and V' cancel because -p*t+s*lambda=0. The remaining coefficient 4-U*p/s=4-s^2(1-s) is positive. On the Alice-rows-2,3 basis (C',Q'), the remaining 2x2 Gram is H=I_2-h*(-t,1)*(-t,1)^*, with h=p^2+s^4/(4U)=(1-s)^2+s/4. Its PSD condition is h*(1+U)<=1. Since U=s^3 and s<=3/4, (1+s^3)*((1-s)^2+s/4)-1 = s*(-7/4+s+s^2-(7/4)*s^3+s^4)<0: s+s^2<=21/16<7/4 and s^3*(s-7/4)<=0. Thus H is PSD. All remaining source terms and every vector in span(C',Q') have SR<=2, proving the exact decomposition uniformly for this whole small-t chart.
bob_and_weighted_extension: R_* is invariant under swapping tensor factors, sending the Alice statement to Bob. Every remaining source generator other than A has SR<=2, so local images of any additional nonnegative sum T of their projectors preserve SN<=2. This proves the alpha*R_*+T extension without assuming T itself is PPT. If the full enlarged source is PPT, local congruences preserve PPT. Any rank-four map with the specified kernel differs from the chosen normal form by an invertible output map; any opposite local map preserves an SR2 decomposition.

exact_check.observed: For both Alice and Bob, t=27/125 gives U=729/15625, s=9/25, p=16/25 and all phase amplitudes rational. The checker verifies every 3x3 minor of eight phase vectors, all 400 output entries, mixed-Gram pivots [38151979/39062500,18636354/38151979], and actual projected PT PSD. It hash-pins/replays the preceding eight complex mixed-tail cases and their upstream checks. Universal t follows from the written coupled-Gram bound and previous chart, not from finite examples.

limits: Only the tail CP1 kernel on at least one subsystem, the indicated 5x5 diagonal cone, and arbitrary opposite local maps are covered. The result does not settle both non-tail/non-coordinate kernels, the unrestricted 4x4 PPT Schmidt problem, an SN>=3 witness, external/formal review or novelty.
